newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ST LUKES PLANS NZ$90 MLN RIGHTS ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: ST LUKES PLANS NZ$90 MLN RIGHTS ISSUE.

text.p: Retail property company St Lukes Group Ltd said on Thursday it planned to seek to raise about NZ$90 million via a rights issue from shareholders.

In a statement accompanying the firm's annual results, it said the fully-underwritten, renounceable rights issue would offer one share and two convertible notes to holders in proportion to every 18 securities (shares and notes) held.

"The capital raised will be used to repay borrowings (33 percent as at June 30) and thereby increase the company's flexibility to pursue future redevelopment, refurbishment and acquisition opportunities with the aim of further enhancing our portfolio of assets and maximising returns to investors," the company said.

The new shares and convertible notes are to be issued on the same terms as existing securities. Up to 20 million shares are to be issued at $1.62 each and up to 40 million convertible notes at $1.44 per note.
A prospectus is expected to be registered on August 22 and delivered to investors in the first week of September, it added.
St Lukes is choosing to stick with the same capital structure as its original offering, meaning it has a substantial number of convertible notes on which it pays interest from its after-tax earnings.
In the year to June 30 the company made a net profit of $31.15 million, up 8.6 percent, spent on net convertible note interest of $13.0 million and net dividends of $18.15 million.
St Lukes said it expected continued rental growth as demand for retail space in regional centres remained firm.

"We are also expecting a continuation of the growth in earnings as a result of the completion of the WestCity redevelopment and from new management initiatives Westfield Holdings are expected to implement," it added.
Australia's Westfield took over commercial management of the St Lukes property portfolio earlier this year.
